title: Per-model deployability sentinel and profile contract for quant defaults
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a deployability sentinel and a machine-readable profile contract for per-model quantization defaults stored in the model catalog. The goal is to prevent silent accuracy regressions when rolling INT8/FP8 profiles by: 1) defining a compact contract that specifies required calibration artifacts, acceptable metric bands, fallback profiles, and rollout constraints, and 2) implementing a lightweight sentinel in the CI/rollout pipeline that validates candidate profiles against the contract and historical baselines before they reach production.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A JSON schema for the per-model quantization profile contract exists and is checked by CI. 2) CI has a 'deployability sentinel' step that runs calibration verification on a sampled validation shard and returns pass/fail. 3) Failed profiles automatically attach a detailed failure report to the PR and block the release. 4) A documented fallback chain is recorded in the catalog and honored by the runtime routing. 5) Observability shows the sentinel's historical pass rate and latency impact.
technical_decision: We will encode the profile contract as a single-file JSON schema (<=5KB) that references calibration dataset fingerprints, numeric metric expectations (e.g., mean BLEU/EM/ROUGE delta and 95th percentile perplexity), runtime quant-mode tags (e.g., 'int8-perf', 'fp8-safe'), and a required 'shadow-eval' directive used by CI. CI will run shadow evals on 1% randomly sampled shard (min 2k tokens) using AWS spot GPU pool. If a profile shows metric regression beyond the contract's thresholds, CI fails and artifacts are stored in an S3 path referenced in the PR comment.
rollout_plan: 1) Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement schema and CI sentinel in staging; run on existing catalog entries in dry-run mode. 2) Phase 2 (1 week): Enable blocking on non-core models with 'canary' tag. 3) Phase 3 (2 weeks): Ramp to all models with monitoring dashboards and automated rollback hooks. 4) Post-deploy: iterate thresholds based on signal noise and false positives.
calibration_workflow_steps: 1. Assemble per-model calibration pack: representative batches, exemplar prompts, and fingerprint metadata.
2. Run calibration harness to produce scale/zero-point candidates for INT8 and dynamic range statistics for FP8.
3. Generate candidate profile and compute per-exemplar metrics versus fp32 baseline.
4. Upload calibration artifacts to catalog storage and sign them with provenance tags.
5. Trigger CI sentinel (shadow-eval) which runs a lightweight accuracy pass and latency smoke test.
6. If sentinel passes, tag profile as 'validated-for-rollout'; otherwise attach failure report and mark 'needs-investigation'.
validation_plan: Validation uses a three-tier approach: 1) Unit-level numeric checks (tensor-level MSE), 2) Sampled shadow-eval with held-out prompts (N=2k min tokens) computing both aggregate and percentile metrics, 3) A/B canary in prod for 24h on 5% traffic comparing user-facing metrics (perplexity proxy and prompt-level exact-match).
Metric thresholds will be conservative initially: e.g., relative delta <= 1.5% mean token-likelihood, 95th percentile perplexity delta <= 5%, and no catastrophic failure cases (runtime OOM or NaN).
Validation artifacts (diff logs, per-example failures, calibration histograms) must be stored and linked in the PR for postmortem.

2025-02-15 Diego Morales: Confirmed that 2k tokens on a single GPU takes ~30-45s for most LLMs; spot pool cost estimated at ~$0.65 per run. Raised concern about CI latency impacting PR throughput.
2025-02-18 Priya Nair (ML Research): Suggested adding per-example error buckets to detect pattern regressions (e.g., hallucination on numerics). Added to schema draft.

2025-02-25 Diego Morales: Implemented a prototype sentinel job in CI; in dry-run against 15 catalog models produced 3 failures; initial failures traced to calibration data drift on two models. Created follow-up ENG-999002.
2025-03-01 QA Review (R. Chen): Reviewed failure reports; requested clearer failure messages and automated recommendations (e.g., 'fallback->fp32' or 'increase-calibration-samples').
2025-03-05 Product Review (L. Gomez): Approved approach; asked to add rollout throttling knobs in Console and a 'snooze' for known noisy models.
